newsitem.title: USA: U.S. net intl investment position widens in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. net intl investment position widens in 1996.

text.p: The United States, already the world's largest debtor, sank deeper into the red in 1996, a Commerce Department report issued on Monday said.

The value of foreigners' investments in the United States last year outstripped U.S. holdings abroad by a net $182.8 billion, partly because of record buying of U.S. Treasury securities by overseas investors seeking higher returns.

At year-end, the United States net international investment position -- the amount that it owed in excess of the value of its foreign holdings -- had deteriorated to $870.5 billion from $687.7 billion a year earlier.

Commerce said big capital inflows from overseas investors as well as losses on foreign exchange for Americans whose overseas assets are denominated in Japanese or European currencies, accounted for much of the deterioration.

The dollar appreciated sharply in value against Japanese and European currencies last year. Thus, not only did the value of foreign holdings shrink, but also any interest or dividend earnings brought home were worth less when they were converted into dollars.
"The increase in the negative position (of the United States) was only partly offset by the greater price appreciation in foreign securities than in U.S. securities," the Commerce Department said.
U.S. Treasury securities were specially attractive to foreigners.
Commerce said that foreigners from the private sector as well as international financial institutions increased their U.S. Treasury security holdings by $141.2 billion to a total of $530.6 billion.

Among the countries that were the sources of the largest direct investments in the United States last year were Britain at $142.6 billion; Japan at $118.1 billion; the Netherlands at $73.8 billion and Canada at $53.8 billion.

The same countries were the key targets for Americans' foreign investment, though not in the same order. The biggest investment totals last year were placed in Britain at $142.6 billion (the same as the amount invested by Britons in the United States); Canada $91.6 billion; the Netherlands $44.7 billion and Japan $39.6 billion.
